# Fixture provenance and limits

These files contain synthetic examples, not user data, verified identities or
working credentials. `adversarial.json` records the rationale for each invalid
document. All stronger labels in valid fixtures demonstrate shape only. The
DSSE envelope uses a deliberately invalid all-zero signature. Public counters
and timestamps are fictional test values.

`core-reference.json` retains the independently recorded S01 Core commit,
source hashes and identity anchor. The raw missing-ID regression is exercised
against Core's real function. No Radar association resolver exists at this step.

`test_primitives.py` transcribes Ed25519 tests 1–3 from
[RFC 8032 §7.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032#section-7.1) and JCS sorting
and serialization examples from
[RFC 8785 §3.2.3–3.2.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785#section-3.2.3).
The Ed25519 seeds are public known-answer test data, not secrets. Never use them
as actual authority keys. The expected bytes are literal reference values, not
generated by the implementation under test.

RFC material: copyright © 2017 (RFC 8032) and © 2020 (RFC 8785), IETF Trust and
the identified authors. See the documents' copyright notices and
[IETF Trust Legal Provisions](https://trustee.ietf.org/documents/trust-legal-provisions/).
No cryptographic implementation code has been copied from the RFCs.

These tests cover primitive interoperability and structural fail-closed rules.
They do not claim representative field accuracy, complete DSSE verification,
trusted provenance, actual OS peer authentication or completed release gates.
